newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to make radio address on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to make radio address on Friday.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin will make a radio address to the nation on Friday, his second since recovering from a bout of pneumonia, his press service said on Thursday.
It declined to say what Yeltsin would say in his address, to be broadcast at 0800 GMT, but Ekho Moskvy radio said he was expected to focus on army reform and the state budget.

The plight of Russia's cash-strapped armed forces has become a hot political issue. Defence Minister Igor Rodionov drew a rebuke from Yeltsin earlier this week for saying he was in charge of "a disintegrating army and a dying navy".

Yeltsin signed the 1997 budget into law on Wednesday after months of parliamentary wrangling. Passing the budget opens the door to the International Monetary Fund agreeing a 1997 economic programme with Russia under a $10 billion three-year loan.
